thesis: The architecture becomes a research program through separately falsifiable claims, strong comparisons, staged learning and explicit failures.
role: Chapters 24–28 specify hypotheses, experiments, objections and progression.

ideas.statement: Exact merging, useful relations, selective ambiguity, interface transfer, learned selection and diagnostic benefit require separate tests and failure criteria.
Formal experiments should vary state size, representation richness, graph topology and algebra independently, using adversarial continuations and full amortized costs.
Language experiments separate interpretation from reasoning, vary minimal pairs and new compositions, test rare exceptions, and report coverage, abstention and proof validity.
Known dynamic programming, hidden primitives, large interfaces and difficult semantic verification are substantive objections; local guarantees cannot be certified global truth.
Progress proceeds from exact finite models through adaptive interfaces, revisable controlled language and transfer to independent real-document evaluation.
Understanding as preserving relevant distinctions remains a philosophical hypothesis; negative results and independent criticism can improve it.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Changing gave to showed or all to some tests meaning-sensitive responses; consistent renaming should not.
Holding the verifier fixed isolates the effect of learned candidate selection.
Diagnostic benefit requires independent evaluators, not confidence in attractive explanations.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Formal correctness may be practically useless, and exhaustive future questions may prevent compression.
Multiple outputs from the same model type are not independent confirmation.

audit.notes: Read every unit; preserve proposed versus demonstrated status.
